extracted.intended_audience: physical education faculty, department administrators, and educational researchers interested in student evaluation methods
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation instrument and administration procedures for assessing collegiate physical education activity courses (Instructional Assessment Inventory) and a study comparing instructor-administered vs. administrator-administered delivery. Includes items, section dimensions, scoring, and procedural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section I - Knowledge, Clarity & Enthusiasm
rubrics_metrics.description: Major inventory section labeled “Knowledge, Clarity and Enthusiasm.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four primary dimensions of the Instructional Assessment Inventory; section scores are summed from individual item responses and analyzed separately and in combination with other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section II - Organization and Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Major inventory section labeled “Organization and Preparation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures planning, use of class time, materials, and safety; section sums are used in composite and section-level analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section III - Instructor - Student Interaction and Rapport
rubrics_metrics.description: Major inventory section labeled “Instructor - Student Interaction and Rapport.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses feedback, fairness, interest in students, and helpfulness; shown to have significant interaction effects with administration procedure in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section IV - General Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Major inventory section labeled “General Evaluation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures overall enjoyment, willingness to enroll/recommend, and overall course/instructor ratings; used with other sections for composite evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1 - The instructor effectively explained or demonstrated the skills of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor effectively explained or demonstrated the skills of the activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options A–E mapped to scores 1–5; item analyzed individually and as part of Section I. Study found significant interaction effects on some individual items by administration procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2 - The instructor was perceptive in diagnosing and skillful in correcting individual errors in performance.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor was perceptive in diagnosing and skillful in correcting individual errors in performance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual item of Section I; ANOVA indicated significant interaction for this item (example result shown in paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3 - The instructor clearly explained the rules, scoring and strategies involved in the activity.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor clearly explained the rules, scoring and strategies involved in the activity. (May not apply to dance, gymnastics, skating, etc.)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I item; respondents choose A–E; applicability note included for certain activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4 - The instructor was enthusiastic and interested in teaching the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor was enthusiastic and interested in teaching the subject matter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I item; captures instructor affect and engagement; scored A–E → 1–5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5 - The instructor demonstrated a comprehensive knowledge of the activity.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor demonstrated a comprehensive knowledge of the activity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I item; shown in study analyses (individual-item interaction significance reported for this item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 6 - The instructor encouraged and motivated you to attain a higher skill level.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor encouraged and motivated you to attain a higher skill level."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I item; measures motivational/encouragement behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 7 - The instructor seemed capable of teaching the more highly skilled performers.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor seemed capable of teaching the more highly skilled performers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section I item; assesses perceived competence across ability levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 8 - The instructor provided, verbally or via a course outline, the course objectives, expectations, assignments, examination information, and grading procedures.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor provided, verbally or via a course outline, the course objectives, expectations, assignments, examination information, and grading procedures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II item; evaluates clarity of course structure and communicated expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9 - The instructor's lessons reflected planned learning sessions and efficient utilization of class time.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor's lessons reflected planned learning sessions and efficient utilization of class time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II item; assesses organization and lesson planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 10 - Within the limitations of the facilities, the instructor provided maximal active participation time for all students.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Within the limitations of the facilities, the instructor provided maximal active participation time for all students."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II item; measures use of facilities and opportunities for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 11 - The textbook and other instructional materials were of value in the course.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The textbook and other instructional materials were of value in the course."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II item; paper reports significant interaction for this item related to administration procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 12 - A safe learning environment was provided for the class.
rubrics_metrics.description: "A Safe learning environment was provided for the class."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section II item; assesses student safety perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 13 - The instructor provided evaluative feedback concerning your skill development.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor provided evaluative feedback concerning your skill development."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section III item; measures feedback quality and frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 14 - The instructor was impartial and fair in dealing with students.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor was impartial and fair in dealing with students."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section III item; evaluates perceived fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 15 - The instructor was interested in you and your skill development.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor was interested in you and your skill development."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section III item; assesses perceived instructor interest in individual students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 16 - The instructor was understanding of and helpful to students who experienced difficulty acquiring the activity skills.
rubrics_metrics.description: "The instructor was understanding of and helpful to students who experienced difficulty acquiring the activity skills."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section III item; shown in study to have significant interaction effects with administration procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 17 - Fun and enjoyment were experienced throughout the course.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Fun and enjoyment were experienced throughout the course."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section IV item; measures affective student response to the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 18 - Based on your experience in this course, would you enroll in another physical education course and/or recommend activity courses to others?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Based on your experience in this course, would you enroll in another physical education course and/or recommend activity courses to others?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section IV item; behavioral-intent/recommendation indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 19 - Considering all aspects of the course, how would you rate this course?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Considering all aspects of the course, how would you rate this course?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section IV item; global course rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 20 - Considering all of the instructional aspects of this course, how would you rate the instructor?
rubrics_metrics.description: "Considering all of the instructional aspects of this course, how would you rate the instructor?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section IV item; global instructor rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response format and scoring (A–E → 1–5; section & composite sums)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each inventory item one of five possible responses (A through E) was selected; each response mapped to scores 1 through 5 (1 = least favorable, 5 = most favorable). Scores were summed for each section and for all twenty items to produce section and composite means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use summed section scores and total composite for group mean comparisons; individual items also analyzed. The study used group means and 2x2 ANOVA on sums and items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration mode: instructor-administered vs. administrator-administered
rubrics_metrics.description: Two administration procedures compared: 'instructor administered' (instructor present, distributes forms, designates a student to collect and forward) versus 'administrator administered' (department chair or associate dean administers the instrument in the instructor's absence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator-administered procedure included explicit assurances of anonymity and an introductory script (see next metric). The study found differential effects: administrator-administered evaluations tended to increase faculty ratings and decrease graduate assistant ratings on certain items/sections; instructor-administered may inflate ratings (supported by cited literature). This administration mode is a critical procedural variable affecting validity of evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator introductory script and assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: When administrator-administered, the administrator (introduced self and position), informed students of activity program enrollments and importance of activity classes, reminded students of the need for evaluative feedback, and assured anonymity of responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These preparatory remarks are part of the administration procedure hypothesized to influence student responses; assuring anonymity is explicitly emphasized as a validity-protecting practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor-administered procedure (usual departmental practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In instructor-administered sections, instructors conducted evaluations according to their usual procedure: distributing forms, designating a student to collect completed forms and forward them to the departmental office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study and cited literature warn this practice can positively influence student ratings through instructor presence and subtle/overt reinforcement; considered a potential source of bias when used for administrative decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of administration
rubrics_metrics.description: All rating forms were administered during the final examination week of Winter Quarter, each student completed the inventory prior to taking the final written examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing (final exam week, before final exam) is a documented procedural detail and may influence results; consistency of timing across sections is implied for comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paired-section experimental design and counterbalancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Twelve instructors who taught paired sections (two sections of the same activity course) participated; each instructor administered the inventory in one paired section while the other section was administrator-administered. In six of the twelve pairs the instructor-administered inventory was given first and in the other six the administrator-administered inventory was given first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paired sections and counterbalanced order control for instructor and order effects; design detail is relevant to interpreting observed administration effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample composition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample comprised twelve instructors (six regular faculty and six graduate assistants), 460 completed inventories across ten different activity courses (archery, badminton, ballet, basketball, billiards, folk dance, gymnastics, modern dance, racquetball, volleyball).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential effects were analyzed by instructor group (faculty vs graduate assistants); population and activity diversity should be considered when generalizing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis conventions used in study
rubrics_metrics.description: The study calculated sums and group means for item sections and the composite; a 2 x 2 ANOVA (instructor group × administration procedure) was used with alpha = .05 to test for significance, and interaction effects were interpreted for differential administrative effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant interaction (e.g., F = 4.55, p = .03) indicates administration procedure affects faculty and graduate assistants differently; non-significant p-values (e.g., p < .06) were described as 'indication' rather than formally significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive caution regarding administration-induced bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature and study discussion warn that instructor presence/administration and deliberate influential tactics (subtle verbal reinforcement or overt rewards) can cause higher student appraisals, and thus results from faculty-administered ratings should be used cautiously for administrative decisions (reappointment, tenure, promotion, salary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Fentress (1973), Sheehan (1975), and others; recommends considering administration mode and anonymity to improve validity of student evaluations.
